newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ says scope for conditions to ease.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ says scope for conditions to ease.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand said on Thursday that monetary conditions had become inappropriately firm and it was looking to see some easing.
Speaking at the release of the bank's latest economic projections Brash said the monetary conditions the bank was seeking had not changed since December.
"However, since December, actual monetary conditions have been firmer than the bank has wanted. In recent weeks, conditions have tightened further and have become inappropriately firm.
"We will be looking to see conditions ease towards those we are seeking," Brash said.
But he said the bank saw no scope for an easing in desired monetary conditions.
The bank's projections showed inflation falling over the coming 12 to 18 months while economic growth was expected to increase.

"There are clear risks that inflation will remain persistently high in some areas (particularly housing) and the impact of the high exchange rate on prices has been unexpectedly weak to date," Brash said.

"Together these factors mean that a cautious approach to determining the stance of moentary policy is appropriate until we can be confident that, after an easing, inflation would still turn down towars the middle of the zero to three percent target range in a clear and sustained manner."
Looking further ahead, the government's tax and spending policies already announced would contribute importantly to a projected rise in inflation in 1998 and 1999.

"The government will need to be mindful of these inflationary risks in setting fiscal policy, particularly if there is no compulsory savings scheme to offset the impact of tax cuts currently planned for the year," Brash said.
